# autario-mcp

<!-- INTRO:START -->
<!-- generated by scripts/check-readme-sync.js from backend/data/entityDescription.json + the hosted server tool list | do not edit manually | run `npm run build-readme` -->

autario is data app infrastructure: your tools and thousands of public datasets in one normalized layer, and the report your AI builds on top of it runs here on a link you share.

**Connect your platforms, then let your assistant interpret the numbers.** Connect your ad accounts, your shop, your web analytics, your social profiles, your CRM and your finance tools on autario once. Through this MCP server your assistant reads those tables, joins them and explains what moved: spend, revenue and ROAS per channel, the audience behind a traffic change, the posts that worked. The public catalogue (World Bank, FRED, Eurostat, OECD, WHO, IMF, SEC) sits next to your own data as context, so a sales dip can be read against inflation or market growth in the same answer.

- **Brands and instances.** Group connected accounts by brand, and pick which accounts (instances) a report reads, so an agency asks about one brand without another brand's numbers in the answer.
- **Numbers the model does not make up.** Report tools return what autario computes server-side from your own tables, and every public value cites its primary source, so the model explains figures instead of recomputing or guessing them.
- **83 tools, each marked read or write.** The Access column in the Tool Reference below comes from each tool's own annotations, so a client can allow the read tools and ask before a write.
- **Remote or local, one tool list.** Point any HTTP MCP client at `https://autario.com/mcp` with no install, or run it over stdio with `npx autario-mcp`. The stdio package is a thin bridge to that same server: it loads the tool list at start, so new and improved tools arrive without updating the package.

<!-- INTRO:END -->

[autario.com](https://autario.com/?utm_source=mcp_readme&utm_medium=hero&utm_campaign=marketplace) | [Developer docs](https://autario.com/developer/docs?utm_source=mcp_readme&utm_medium=hero&utm_campaign=marketplace) | [Get an API Key](https://autario.com/account?utm_source=mcp_readme&utm_medium=hero&utm_campaign=marketplace&tab=apikeys)

## Why autario-mcp

- **Your platforms, not just public data.** Ads, shop, analytics, social, CRM and finance connectors land in tables your assistant can query, join and compare, and `marketing_report`, `social_360` and the other report tools return the same numbers the app shows.
- **No hallucinated numbers.** Every value is sourced from a known publisher and cited back to a primary URL. Use `verify_value` to double-check any claim.
- **Cross-dataset joins, no setup.** Indicators across different datasets share `autario_time` + `autario_entity` shadow columns, so `get_entity_data(USA, [gdp, unemployment, life_expectancy])` returns one wide table, joined automatically.
- **Statistical primitives built-in.** `correlate`, `regression`, `find_drivers`, `lag_analysis`, `seasonality_decomposition` and more, with effect sizes, p-values, and plain-language interpretations.
- **Charts that persist.** `publish_chart` writes a Plotly spec to autario.com. The result is a permanent, embeddable URL like `autario.com/chart/{slug}` | the LLM builds the spec, autario pulls real rows for it, no hallucinated data path.
- **LLM-agnostic.** Works with Claude, GPT, Gemini, local models | anything that speaks MCP.

## Quick Demo

Install the server, then ask your assistant questions like these. The model picks the right tools and answers with cited data.

```text
Ask:    "Why did ROAS drop last week for this brand? Compare Meta Ads and Google Ads
         against Shopify revenue."
Tools:  get_my_workspace -> marketing_report
Output: Spend, revenue and ROAS per channel against the previous period, from the
        connected accounts of that brand only.
```

```text
Ask:    "What drives US inflation? Look at money supply, oil prices, and unemployment."
Tools:  list_indicators -> find_drivers
Output: Ranked drivers with r, p-value, R squared per candidate.
```

```text
Ask:    "Compare life expectancy in Germany, USA and Japan from 2000 to 2023, then publish a chart."
Tools:  compare_entities -> publish_chart
Output: Wide-format table joined on year, plus a permanent autario.com/chart/{slug} URL.
```

```text
Ask:    "Is consumer confidence a leading indicator of US retail sales?"
Tools:  lag_analysis
Output: Cross-correlation peak at lag k, with interpretation in months.
```

```text
Ask:    "Find a dataset on unemployment, build me a small app that charts it for
         Germany, publish it as unlisted and give me the link."
Tools:  search_datasets -> get_dataset_schema -> create_app ->
        update_app_manifest -> upload_app_bundle -> get_app_preview_url -> publish_app
Output: A live URL you own. No review queue, no waiting list, nobody to ask.
```

## Install

### Claude Desktop, Cursor, Cline (stdio)

`~/.config/claude/claude_desktop_config.json` on Mac/Linux, `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json` on Windows.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "autario": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["autario-mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Restart your client. On launch the package connects to `https://autario.com/mcp` and prints one line to stderr: the tool count and whether it is signed in with your API key.

**The package updates itself.** Since 3.0.0 `autario-mcp` carries no tool of its own: it is a small bridge that loads the tool list from the hosted server at start and forwards every call there. New tools and improved descriptions reach you with the next restart of your client, without `npm update`. It needs a network connection; offline, it prints one line saying so and exits.

### Claude Web, OpenAI Custom GPTs, any HTTP MCP client

Point your client at the hosted endpoint. No install needed.

```text
URL:        https://autario.com/mcp
Transport:  Streamable HTTP (POST /mcp)
```

The hosted endpoint also supports MCP prompts: `analyze-dataset`, `create-chart`, `compare-countries`.

### Enable your own data and the write tools

Add API credentials to the stdio config or send them as `x-api-key` / `x-api-secret` headers to the HTTP endpoint. The stdio package sends them as those same headers, and every tool then runs as you. A key the server does not accept stops the start with one line that says so.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "autario": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["autario-mcp"],
      "env": {
        "AUTARIO_API_KEY":    "your_key",
        "AUTARIO_API_SECRET": "your_secret"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Get keys at [autario.com/account](https://autario.com/account?utm_source=mcp_readme&utm_medium=install&utm_campaign=marketplace&tab=apikeys).

## Your own data: connectors

Ask your assistant about your own accounts, not only public statistics. A connector reads one service read-only into private tables you own; the assistant reads those tables with the same tools it uses for the public catalog.

Connector families: ads (Meta Ads, Google Ads, TikTok Ads, LinkedIn Ads, Microsoft Advertising, Pinterest, Snapchat, Reddit, Amazon Ads), shops and marketplaces (Shopify, WooCommerce, Shopware, Magento, BigCommerce, Amazon, eBay, Etsy and more), web analytics and search (Google Analytics, Search Console, Bing Webmaster Tools, Plausible, Matomo, PostHog), social (Facebook Pages, Instagram, LinkedIn, YouTube, TikTok, Threads), email, support and reviews (Klaviyo, Mailchimp, Zendesk, Trustpilot), CRM and finance (HubSpot, Salesforce, Stripe, Wise, invoicing tools) and AI usage (OpenAI, Anthropic and others). The full, current list with one page per connector: [autario.com/connectors](https://autario.com/connectors?utm_source=mcp_readme&utm_medium=connectors&utm_campaign=marketplace).

Three steps:

1. Connect a service on its page, for example `https://autario.com/connectors/shopify`: sign in or paste a key, tick the reports you want. The first refresh starts right away and then runs daily.
2. Add autario to your assistant once: `claude mcp add autario --transport http https://autario.com/mcp`, or a custom connector with that address in Claude or ChatGPT, or the stdio config above with your API key.
3. Ask in plain words, for example "Which products sold the most units on Shopify last month, and how much revenue did each bring in?"

Behind that question the assistant calls `list_connectors` (what is connected, one `dataset_id` per report), `get_dataset_schema` (the columns and what each one means) and `query_dataset` (only the rows and columns the question needs). Nothing in a connector writes to the connected account.

### Build and Ship a Data App (requires AUTARIO_API_KEY)

Build an app that runs ON autario and publish it yourself on a paid plan: a content check runs on every publish and a store listing gets one AI content review per version, synchronously, no queue. The path is create_app -> update_app_manifest -> upload_app_bundle (or write_app_artifact) -> get_app_preview_url -> publish_app, and every response carries a `next_step`. Each tool is a thin wrapper over the same REST endpoint an outside developer calls directly, so an agent is exactly its owner and never more.

| Tool | Access | What it does | Parameters |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `create_app` | write | Create a data app on autario in ONE call, owned by you. ## autario.js: the data SDK inside every app

An app you ship with `create_app` or `upload_app_bundle` runs in a locked sandbox with no network. It reads data with `autario.js`, which autario inlines into every app it serves (a `<script src="https://autario.com/autario.js"></script>` tag is optional). Every call runs as the person looking at the app, with that person's role: the owner and the team members the owner invited (reader, editor, admin) see the datasets the app declares; a stranger sees public catalog data only. No key or token ever reaches the app.

```html
<script src="https://autario.com/autario.js"></script>
<script>
  (async () => {
    const { app, user } = await autario.ready();          // user.role: owner | admin | editor | reader | visitor; user.id is anonymous per app
    const [first] = await autario.datasets();             // the datasets this app declares
    const rows = await autario.query(first.id, { limit: 10, orderBy: 'date desc' });
    await autario.artifacts.set('last_view', { id: first.id });   // editor or higher
  })();
</script>
```

Declare the user's own tables with `create_app` `datasets: [ids]`. Full reference: [autario.com/developer/docs/autario-js](https://autario.com/developer/docs/autario-js).

## Environment Variables

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AUTARIO_API_KEY` | _unset_ | Your own data, connectors and the write tools. Public read tools work without it. |
| `AUTARIO_API_SECRET` | _unset_ | Companion secret for the API key. |
| `AUTARIO_MCP_URL` | `https://autario.com/mcp` | The MCP endpoint the stdio bridge connects to. Override only for your own autario server. |
| `AUTARIO_API_URL` | `https://autario.com` | An autario base URL; the bridge connects to its `/mcp`. Kept from 2.x, `AUTARIO_MCP_URL` wins when both are set. |

## Data Sources

World Bank, FRED, Eurostat, OECD, IMF, ECB, WHO, US Census Bureau, plus user-contributed datasets. Every dataset record includes a `source_url` pointing back to the primary publisher. Live catalog: [autario.com/data](https://autario.com/data?utm_source=mcp_readme&utm_medium=sources&utm_campaign=marketplace).

## Development

This package is part of the [autario monorepo](https://github.com/autario/autario). The published package is `server.js` + `bridge.js`: a stdio MCP server that proxies `initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call` and prompts to the hosted server. Tool definitions and handlers live only on the server (`tools.js` and its parts, served by `remote.js`), and the Tool Reference section above is generated from the list that server answers.

```bash
# regenerate the README Tool Reference from the server tool list
npm run build-readme

# verify README is in sync (used in CI)
npm run check-readme
```
